root.name: Grünfeld Defense: Makogonov Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. e3 O-O 6. b4

overview: In the Three Knights Grünfeld White plays 6.b4, the Makogonov idea, to gain queenside space and cramp the ...c5 break. Black usually hits the centre at once with ...c5 or ...dxc4 followed by ...b5 and ...a5, while White keeps a pawn centre and puts the bishops on b2 and e2. The play is a strategic fight over White space against Black counterplay on the queenside.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with b4 and b2-bishop pressure on d4 and the long diagonal
Hold the centre with e3, Bd3 and O-O

black_ideas.idea: Strike the centre with ...c5 or ...dxc4 and ...b5

typical_structures.structure: White pawns b4, c4, d4, e3 against Black ...c5 break
Queenside space versus pressure on d4

character.notes: A controlled space fight rather than a race; pieces are slowly rearranged.

soundness.notes: A respected anti-Grünfeld set-up used by strong players.

structure.notes: The d4/c4 centre is tense and Black hits it from both sides.

approach.notes: A system-like plan for White against the Grünfeld but used mainly as a sideline.

level.notes: Plans over the b4 and ...c5 trade-offs matter more than memorised moves.

character.reason: The play is strategic and neither side takes early risks, but it is not especially hard to break down.

gambit.reason: Any pawn taken on c4 comes straight back.

structure.reason: The d4 and c4 pawns are in tension with ...c5 and ...dxc4 still to come.

approach.reason: A sideline of the Grünfeld that strong players use but not a system against everything.

level.reason: Black needs to grasp the ...c5 and ...a5 plans but there is little forced theory.

plans.reason: White gains queenside space with b4.
